title: Active Inference and Predictive Processing for Skill Learning: Implications for Skill Acquisition in Coaching Practice.
abstract: This paper explores the potential of the Active Inference Framework (AIF) and Predictive Processing (PP) to advance our understanding of skill and motor learning with a key focus on introducing these concepts to coaches and highlighting their practical implications. Conceptual frameworks such as Information Processing (IP) and Ecological Dynamics (ED) have contributed significantly to the field of skill acquisition. Despite recent efforts to reconcile these perspectives, however, their fundamentally different theoretical foundations concerning perception, cognition and learning processes pose substantial challenges for integration. Although ED has made valuable contributions through its focus on perception-action coupling and direct interaction with the environment, it involves adopting a radical ontological stance that emphasises rejecting traditional cognitive constructs that can complicate practical applications in coaching. Conversely, IP's reliance on concepts such as stored motor programs and the view of the brain as a computer-like processor can limit its ability to account for the dynamic, emergent nature of skill acquisition in real-world contexts. We suggest that AIF offers a parsimonious perspective, accommodating the dynamic, embodied and enactive nature of skill acquisition without the necessity of committing to either framework's specific assumptions. This perspective provides practitioners with a coherent and flexible framework for understanding and designing skill learning interventions, offering a practically useful account of skill acquisition for coaching practice.
summary: Artículo conceptual que presenta el marco de Inferencia Activa y Procesamiento Predictivo para entender el aprendizaje de habilidades, contrastándolo con el procesamiento de información y la dinámica ecológica, y lo traduce para entrenadores.
why: Entra de lleno en el debate teórico ecológico vs. representacional sobre la adquisición de habilidades.
practice: Ofrece pautas para diseñar la práctica pensando en cómo el jugador anticipa y reduce la incertidumbre.

title: Mismatches Between Talent Identification and Development Models: Why Their Distinct Natures Must Be Nurtured.
venue: Perspectives on psychological science : a journal of the Association for Psychological Science
abstract: The identification and development of talent are top priorities across education, sports, business, and the arts. A major challenge lies in developing and applying appropriate models in both science and practice. Talent-identification models should center around predicting future excellence, whereas talent-development models should focus on how skills, resources, and their interactions change over time on the path to excellence. After providing an overview of the literature on talent-identification and talent-development models, I will argue that these models are often misapplied across domains: Talent-identification models are frequently used for talent development, and vice versa, which hampers progress in both scientific research and practical application. To address this issue, I propose a dual-path approach to nurture the distinct natures of talent-identification and talent-development models. For talent development, longitudinal processes involving relevant variables (e.g., psychosocial, cognitive, and physical) should be studied and evaluated at the individual level. For talent identification, predictive models incorporating relevant variables need to be tested, and their optimal and consistent application in real-world settings should be evaluated. This dual-path approach offers opportunities to advance psychological science and practice in identifying and developing talent across diverse domains of achievement.
summary: Perspectiva de Den Hartigh que argumenta que los modelos de identificación del talento (predicción) y de desarrollo (proceso) tienen naturalezas distintas y no deben confundirse.
why: Den Hartigh trabaja el talento desde los sistemas dinámicos; clave para enmarcar el desarrollo como proceso no lineal.
practice: Invita a separar en las academias los criterios de selección de los de formación.

title: Visual Search Strategies and Decision-Making in Highly Trained Female Youth Basketball Players: A Quasi-Experimental in Situ Study of Gaze Behavior during Pick-and-Roll Plays
abstract: This study explored how U16 female basketball players direct their visual attention and make decisions during side pick-and-roll situations under realistic game conditions. Twelve experienced players participated in 4v4 scenarios, where defensive strategies were systematically varied to reflect authentic tactical challenges. Using Pupil Core eye-tracking glasses operating at 120 Hz, we recorded gaze behavior without restricting natural movement on the court. Gaze data were synchronized with nine predefined tactical areas of interest using the surface tracker plugin, enabling detailed analysis of visual search behavior in dynamic environments. Time-series, entropy, and gaze transition analyses revealed that offensive decisions were closely shaped by defensive constraints. “Pass to Roller” and “Pass to Corner” were the most frequent responses, depending on the defensive strategy in place. Players’ gaze patterns evolved throughout each trial, with final fixations on decision targets occurring mainly in the last phase of action preparation. Focused visual strategies were more common in shooting and passing decisions, whereas broader search behavior’s characterized driving actions. These findings show that young players adapt their visual attention on a moment-to-moment basis in response to tactical demands, and support the relevance of in situ eye-tracking as a tool for understanding perception and decision-making in youth basketball.
summary: Estudio cuasi-experimental con jugadoras U16 de baloncesto en situaciones 4v4 de pick-and-roll lateral que analiza la búsqueda visual y la toma de decisiones al variar sistemáticamente la defensa.
why: Diseño representativo de tareas manipulando restricciones del oponente (coautor: Pedro T. Esteves).
practice: Modelo transferible al fútbol: variar la conducta defensiva para educar la atención en acciones combinadas.

title: From talent labels to stable expertise.
abstract: Early achievement and subjective labeling can be a weak guide to sustained expertise. Yet talent labels shape access to coaching, practice, and competition, so selection alters the conditions under which early judgements are later evaluated. This Perspective article proposes a conceptual framework in which labeling, selection, development, transition, and stabilisation are recursively linked processes. Its outcome, stable expertise, is repeated superior, domain-specific performance over a prespecified period that includes substantive changes in performance demands. The central claim is that the same outcome may reflect restricted opportunity, limited learning, difficulty adapting to new demands, or difficulty maintaining an established standard. Distinguishing these explanations requires separate observations of judgements, opportunity allocation, capacity change, adaptation, and performance over time. Five falsifiable propositions, each paired with a prospective design, specify when early indicators should lose predictive value, how selection shapes capacity through allocated opportunities, which junior advantages are unlikely to persist, and how adaptation, regulation, and support sustain or restore expert performance. The evidence is drawn mainly from sport; other domains require their own measures and tests. For talent systems, the framework implies treating labels as provisional predictions, reassessed against the opportunities they have created.
summary: Artículo de perspectiva que propone un marco en el que el etiquetado temprano del talento, la selección y el desarrollo se retroalimentan y condicionan la pericia futura.
why: Aporta una visión de sistema (bucles de retroalimentación) al desarrollo del talento.

title: Decision-Making in Basketball: The Interplay between Cognitive Processes and Motor Execution
abstract: This study aimed to explore the relationship between dribbling behavior preceding passing and shooting patterns, and its implications for the interplay between decision-making efficiency and motor execution across four competitive basketball levels: the National Basketball Association (NBA), the EuroLeague, and European national teams, and the under-16 (U16) and under-18 (U18) European national teams. A total of 32 games (eight from each level) were analyzed to identify performance variables associated with success. Actions involving zero dribbles and sequences of three or more dribbles (3+) emerged as the most effective offensive patterns, reflecting the complementarity between rapid, intuitive decisions and deliberate, well-planned actions. Moreover, at the higher competitive levels, assists were more frequently produced following zero-dribble situations, underscoring the efficiency of quick, collective ball movement among elite players. Professional players were more likely to draw fouls during extended dribbling sequences, suggesting greater technical adaptability compared to lower competitive level players. Overall, these findings emphasize the integration of decision-making and motor execution as hallmarks of basketball expertise, highlighting the importance of developing both intuitive and deliberate decision processes in training.
summary: Analiza la relación entre el bote previo al pase o tiro y la eficiencia decisional en cuatro niveles competitivos de baloncesto (NBA, Euroliga y ligas nacionales).

title: When the Clock Is Wrong
abstract: Section: Preprints Categories: Sport Science, Elite Athletics, Measurement Keywords: soccer, athlete tracking, Sports events, data quality, performance monitoring, synchronisation Practitioners increasingly link coded match events to positional data to quantify the physical demands of individual actions, yet event timestamps are not perfectly aligned with tracking data. This study quantified how this misalignment affects event-level external load flags. Three elite German football matches (3,561 events, 61 players) with frame-level, hand-annotated event times served as ground truth. Four timestamp conditions were compared: the raw provider feed, a best-case constant clock correction and two synchronisation algorithms ( ETSY and ELASTIC ). Speed and acceleration flags were derived for the acting player in a ±2 s window and evaluated on 3,186 common events. Raw timestamps were misaligned by a median of 0.76 s, with 39.2% of events misaligned by more than 1 s. Using raw timestamps, 18.5% (95% CI 13.9–23.8%) of sprint-linked and 27.9% (24.4–31.4%) of sustained-acceleration-linked events were missed, and each additional second of error increased the odds of a missed flag 2.6- to 4.9-fold. A constant clock correction gave no significant improvement because errors were event-specific, whereas ELASTIC reduced misses to 1.0–2.1% (all p < 0.001). Event-level physical metrics should therefore be computed only after validated synchronisation.
summary: Preprint que muestra que las marcas temporales de los eventos codificados no siempre están sincronizadas con los datos posicionales en fútbol, lo que sesga el cálculo de demandas de acciones individuales.
why: Calidad de los datos de tracking, base de los análisis de comportamiento colectivo.
practice: Revisar la sincronización eventos-tracking antes de sacar conclusiones de carga o táctica.

title: Comparison of automated and manual performance analysis tools in amateur padel: a descriptive case study
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Background Automated match-analysis systems increasingly provide technical-tactical reports in padel, but their agreement with manual observation remains unclear. The aim was to describe discrepancies between aggregate match statistics displayed by Padmi and manual observational coding in amateur padel. Methods Three amateur male matches involving one focal player were retrospectively analysed from video using the Padmi app (version 1.3). Six shot types (forehand, backhand, forehand volley, backhand volley, bandeja, smash) and three outcome categories were coded manually and compared with Padmi's aggregate reports. Signed and absolute differences were calculated for shot frequencies and percentage-point differences for outcomes. Shot-level agreement metrics were not calculated because raw Padmi event-level data were unavailable. Results Manual coding identified 891 shots, whereas Padmi displayed 757 (−15.0%). Padmi displayed fewer shots in all matches (−11.4% to −19.2%). Discrepancies varied by shot type: forehand −28.3%, backhand −20.0%, bandeja −3.5%, smash −44.8%, forehand volley +27.2%, backhand volley +5.9%. Overall outcome distributions were similar, but larger shot-specific discrepancies emerged for the smash, bandeja, and forehand volley. Conclusions Padmi's user-facing aggregate statistics differed from manual coding in this small case study. Automated reports may be useful for broad feedback but require cautious interpretation and further independent validation for detailed technical-tactical decisions.
summary: Compara herramientas automáticas y observación manual en el análisis de rendimiento de pádel amateur.
why: Fiabilidad de herramientas de análisis automatizado.

title: Differences in the external and internal load according to the player’s position Diferencias en la carga externa e interna en función de la posición de juego Diferenças na carga externa e interna consoante a posição de jogo
abstract: Background/Objectives: the load analysis in football has consolidated as an essential factor for optimising performance and reducing the injury risk in players at different competitive levels. External and internal loads in football present significant changes according to the player position, and these differences must be considered in the training plan and periodization of the load during the season and in injury prevention. The study aimed to evaluate and compare external, internal, and neuromuscular load in senior football players in Portugal across different players’ positions. Methods: Wimu ProTM (Hudl, Nebraska, United States) and Garmin Heart Rate bands (Garmin International Inc., Kansas, USA) were used to quantify and evaluate the external and internal load of the players. A total of 121 athletes were assessed which were divided into 5 player positions. Results: significant differences were observed between players’ positions across several external and neuromuscular load variables (p >0.001). Considering the distance, midfields reported higher mean values (118.20±12.41) compared to the other positions. Considering the Player Load, significant differences were reported among the different positions (p <0.001; ε² = 0.285) and Total Impacts/min (p <0.001; ε² = 0.312). Regarding the internal load (heart rate), a significant difference was observed for the variable Avg. HR (bpm) (p = 0.024; ε² = 0.062) when comparing GK with all the other positions. In the same line, the GKs were those who reflected the lowest values according to the Avg. HR. Conclusions: the inclusion of kinematics, neuromuscular, and cardiac variables allows the coaching staff a higher comprehension of the sports performance and facilitates the decision-making of the performance manager.
summary: Diferencias de carga externa e interna según la posición del jugador en fútbol.
why: Contexto físico del fútbol por demarcaciones.
practice: Ajustar la carga de las tareas según la posición.
